gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the OREI extender splitters use one EDID setting, chosen on a dial or copied from one display, to tell the source what single format to send, and their pages say nothing about scaling. J-Tech says its JTECH-14EX60-AE 'supports 4K > 1080P downscaling feature on the receiver end, so that users can utilize different resolution monitors within their setup'.
standout_why: I read the two cited OREI pages (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K) and the top-ranked uncited page (UHD14-EX115-K). All three only say to 'Use EDID management when there is no video, wrong resolution, audio compatibility issue, or mixed display capability'. They list single presets (1080p up to 4K60 4:4:4 HDR) or 'copy EDID' from one output, and none mentions scaling or downscaling. The point that the CAT runs cannot go through a network switch is already on both cited pages ('This is not an AV-over-IP system'), so it is not a gap. ChatGPT's J-Tech card did list '4K downscaling', but no page it got explains why a house with mixed TVs needs it.
decides: The setup to check is one 4K source feeding a mix of 4K TVs and older 1080p TVs. With the OREI kits, the source sends one format to every receiver, set by the EDID dial or copied from one display. A 4K preset can leave a 1080p TV with no picture, and a 1080p preset makes every TV 1080p. My conclusion, not a maker quote: J-Tech's receiver-end 4K>1080p downscale is the only feature among ChatGPT's three picks that lets both kinds of TV share a source. That makes the JTECH-14EX60-AE the pick for mixed-TV homes, and either OREI kit is fine when every TV is 4K. Note that J-Tech's own store lists the JTECH-14EX60-AE as not available on 2026-11-10.
